classification.difficultyReason: Several angle relationships must be connected across a zigzag with parallel end segments.

spec.description: Five connected segments with parallel first and last segments, alternating labelled angles and a right-angle square.
spec.mathematics: Consecutive marked angles are 90°, 110°, 115° and alpha; the first and last segments are parallel.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the source givens and alpha are visible.

answer.short:
$\alpha=95^\circ$.

Use parallel auxiliary lines and supplementary angles.
answer.worked:
Draw through each bend a line parallel to the first and last segments. Transfer angles using corresponding or alternate angles. At the first peak, the angle between the incoming segment and the auxiliary parallel is $90^\circ$, leaving an angle $x$ between the outgoing segment and that parallel.
$$\begin{align*}x&=110^\circ-90^\circ\\x&=20^\circ\end{align*}$$
At the next trough, the angle on the other side of its auxiliary parallel is $y$.
$$\begin{align*}y&=115^\circ-20^\circ\\y&=95^\circ\end{align*}$$
The final segment is parallel to the auxiliary line, so $\alpha=y=95^\circ$ by alternate angles.
